note: Adapted from the identification record of De Luna, Su & Scheffrahn (2026), originally in English; that work is a new record, and the morphological characters are a check against the original description by Roisin & Pasteels (1996); the measurement table was not within the excerpted section, so only qualitative characters and the left mandible index are recorded.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Species-level identification rests on the combination of soldier and worker characters. Soldier monomorphic, head capsule orange with the nasus darker, the sides and posterior margin of the head slightly flattened; mandibles with an apical point; antennae 12-segmented, segment 3 the thinnest; nasus with 4 long setae at the base, 4 on the vertex and 2 on each side, situated laterally, plus scattered short hairs. Workers dimorphic, the major worker with a left mandible index of 0.45.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule orange, the nasus darker; sides and posterior margin of the head slightly flattened; mandibles with an apical point; antennae 12-segmented, segment 3 the thinnest; nasus with 4 long setae at the base, 4 on the vertex, 2 on each side and situated laterally, with numerous short hairs scattered among them.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Workers dimorphic. Major worker with a left mandible index of 0.45; the mandibular dentition, the enteric valve (EVA) structure and the gut configuration all agree with the generic characters. Mixed segment long; the mesenteric band of the midgut lies on the outer side of the gut loop and is connected to the rest of the midgut by a wide dorsal stalk; colon long, arising from the apex of the paunch and running posteriorly, then forming a three-dimensional S shape made up of two 180° bends, first anteriorly and then downward, the terminal portion running nearly straight to the rectum. The long colon is a diagnostic character of the genus.
